$comment: Every field a host has lives inside the `host:` object itself, `name` included -- 'these are properties of a host object, it makes no sense for it to be anything otherwise' (a real objection to an earlier flat draft, where `host: <name>` put the name on the header line and every other field as a top-level sibling). os/size/disk are required only when there is no `extends` -- an extending host inherits them from its base (the loader deep-merges the base in; a missing inherited field is then caught at load time). This schema rule stops a standalone host from omitting them by mistake.

host.description: A host: a full VM the builder deploys. See `container:` for the same idea deployed as a container instead. Lives in `hosts/`, reused across environments by name -- it never mentions a network or an address itself, only an environment's topology attaches it to one.

name.description: Unique name for this host, referenced from an environment's topology and from other objects' `depends_on`. Not a hostname -- the environment's `as` field on each copy sets the actual hostname.

os.description: Abstract OS name (e.g. "ubuntu22", "windows-server-2022", "kali"). Each builder config maps this to a concrete image for its hoster, so the same host works on any hoster.

size.description: Abstract size name (e.g. "small", "medium", "large"). Each builder config maps this to concrete CPU/memory for its hoster.

ports.description: TCP/UDP ports this host listens on.

depends_on.description: Other hosts, containers, or networks that must be fully configured (finished building) before this host's own steps run. The host's box is still created ahead of time -- only its steps wait -- e.g. a workstation's domain-join step waits until its domain controller is actually a working DC, not just a booted Windows box. Names the object, not one specific copy: every copy of that object within the same team is waited on. This host's own network is always waited on implicitly.
depends_on.example: depends_on: [domain-controller, prod]   # a host, and a network

steps.description: The ordered steps this host runs after it's provisioned. Each one is exactly one of the action kinds below, plus an optional `validate` block. For anything recurring or time-based, use `schedule:` instead -- steps run once, in order; they were never meant to hold recurring work.

schedule.description: Recurring or anchor-relative triggers for this host, independent of `steps:`'s own order -- each entry fires on its own clock, per its `when:`.
schedule.example:
schedule:
  - when: Every 30 minutes
    script: reboot
  - when: 30 minutes before access closes
    run: systemctl restart nginx

vars.description: Key/value data available to this host's own scripts, on top of whatever cascades down from its environment and network.

tags.description: Labels for searching, grouping, and ad-hoc targeting.

findings.description: Findings that belong to this host specifically.
findings.example:
findings:
  - severity: 4
    difficulty: 2
    description: SQL injection in the login form

extends.description: Name of another host this one extends. The base is deep-merged in: scalar fields (os/size/disk) the child sets win, otherwise they're inherited; vars/tags merge key-by-key (child wins a clash); steps, people and ports are the base's followed by the child's. `os`/`size`/`disk` become optional here since they're inherited.
